title: Run the study and record deviations
summary: Check the whole collection route, preserve the declared denominator and document deviations.
steps: Pilot the exact version-pinned links, instructions, consent, assignment, keyboard flow and supported devices. Check comparable tasks and scoring for every design, including tracking unavailable and interrupted-session cases.

Use the field list generated for this study and its actual Qualtrics route. Do not invent fields or mix the two-survey link route with the embedded one-survey route. For the embedded route, do not also import a separate Survey 1.
Check that a success signal represents the intended behavior. A fired click event is not automatically comprehension or task success. Record self-report and tracker status separately.

Track recruited, eligible, assigned, task-scored and follow-up-completed counts separately. Runner counts are session-based; repeat sessions may be the same person. Check recruitment controls in the approved system without sending identifiers to an agent.

Keep the declared primary denominator. The standard A/B success rate includes everyone assigned: dropout and unmeasured sessions count as not successful. That is a rate convention, not proof of an observed task failure. Separately report missing measurement, dropout and measured-finisher rates; do not replace the primary rate with the most favorable one.

Investigate tracking differences, unequal dropout and version problems before interpreting a comparison. Preserve the original records in approved storage; log technical pauses, restarts, exclusions and protocol changes with their reasons and possible bias.
Follow the predefined stopping rule; do not stop because a preferred result appeared. Technical pauses are documented deviations, not a new opportunity to choose a favorable stopping point.

Keep raw Qualtrics/Medallia exports, participant labels, identifiers and session notes in approved systems. Use the existing approved local analysis workflow. Servant does not fetch survey responses; method-guide sync does not authorize transferring raw data to a model.
questions: Have both normal and broken collection paths been tested?
Are missing measurements distinguished from observed failures without changing the primary denominator?
What changed during fieldwork, and how could that affect the result?
example: If B stops recording success signals, pause and investigate. Keep those assigned sessions in the predeclared primary rate as not successful; label their measurement status unknown or unavailable, not observed task failure. Report the defect and any resulting limits or exclusions transparently.
